Then GREEN: make the bind-on-resume refuse to file a spine path that session_view_provenance already attributes to a DIFFERENT binding key, and refuse to overwrite that attribution. Guard the writer, not the reader -- do not add a third reader-side term.

why_trail.why: The floor is the handoff's, so nothing moved under me. B5's mechanism restated from the code: decide_session_start leaves spine=None on TWO routes -- owns nothing visible (B4, already guarded by 'not owned') and owns an entry whose spine does not load (archived/deleted/no spine field). Both fall into the SAME bind-on-resume write, which files binding[bare sid] -> the single in-tree spine the glob turns up, even when session_view_provenance already attributes that path to a sibling's composite key. So the guard belongs at the writer: refuse to file a path the store already attributes to a different binding key.

GREEN by one writer-side rule, not a third reader term: _attributed_to_another_key(owners, own_spine_path, sid) refuses the bind-on-resume when session_view_provenance already attributes that path to a different binding key, and returns {} so the withholding does not fall through into rendering the very gate it refused to file. Paths compared with _same_path; unusable input answers 'refuse', which is the fail-safe direction at a writer. Targeted class 18 -> 21 green; test_spine_rail.py + test_worktree_derivation.py 191 passed/1 skipped.

No door was traded for another and no pre-existing claim was weakened: the test-file diff has ZERO deletions, so the 18 earlier tests are literally the same text, and the production delta stripped of comments is one new function plus a two-line call. The #202 test survives BECAUSE the guard is narrower than tc1: it fires only on an existing CONFLICTING attribution, and #202 scans up a spine attributed to nobody, so the guard never sees it. That was the stop condition I was told to return on, and it did not trigger.

The lane's recurring defect is a sentence that keeps its shape after the code moves out from under it, so every repair here was made by reading the sentence against the code rather than against the sentence next to it -- and two of the six are test NAMES, which is where the reviewer put the worst placement of this defect. Two names asserted universals ('never', 'only') that this gate's own measurement falsifies; both now state the fixture instead. The refusal enumeration is measured rather than argued: 6 reachable cells, 1 moves.

Full suite 3190 passed / 5 skipped / 1216 subtests / exit 0, cache cleared and SPINE_*/CREW_SCRATCH_DIR scrubbed; '^FAILED' distribution derived mechanically and EMPTY, stated as empty rather than omitted. Every number reconciles against the diff by NAME rather than by count, which is what catches a quiet deletion: two names disappear and both are renames I declared, with the replacements present.

Result artifact written at the path the handoff names, Return status lowercase 'complete'. One claim in the draft (the gauge writer's answer for a refused session) was measured before shipping rather than asserted, and the measurement corrected it: HEAD gives the restarting parent a gauge path inside the CREW's work area, AFTER leaves only its own. Correcting it in place is the same discipline the prose criterion is about.
